correctness.rationale: For H_0=6I-adjacency on Z^3 the exact rank-two equation has determinant 1-lambda^2(G_0(kappa)^2-G_r(kappa)^2). Both positive factors G_0±G_r are strictly decreasing, yielding one simple negative eigenvalue iff lambda>lambda_c. Reflection about the defect midpoint followed by the bipartite sign operator gives H conjugate to 12-H. At lambda_c the threshold Green state has a nonzero k=0 numerator, hence is Fourier L1 but not L2. The free resolvent defect is sqrt(kappa)/(4pi), and the lattice Green far field is 1/(4pi|r|), giving respectively the explicit quadratic gap constant and the inverse-square excess threshold. The exact nearest-neighbor identity g-h_e1=1/6 and independent standard-library numerical checks corroborate normalization; numerical tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: Inspected primary works treat either the rank-one impurity, a quasi-momentum two-particle lattice problem, or a centered fully symmetric multi-delta shell. The accessible earlier local ledger has the two-dimensional neutral pair where binding occurs at every strength, so its implication does not cover a positive three-dimensional threshold or asymptotic distance penalty. Database semantic searches using aliases, parameters, threshold behavior and opposite-sign terminology did not retrieve an exact theorem covering the arbitrary-separation one-attractive/one-repulsive pair. Absence of a search hit is not asserted as a proof of novelty; broader 2009 work remains a stated residual priority risk.

value.rationale: For an experimentally interpretable neutral attractive-repulsive pair in the 3D cubic tight-binding model, the theorem sharply classifies the number of out-of-band states at all strengths and separations, identifies true band-edge resonances, and quantifies both the quadratic detachment and the universal 1/|r|² screening cost compared with an isolated defect. This is a motivated spectral boundary separating 2D unconditional binding from 3D finite threshold, rather than a renamed textbook result or arbitrary numerical slice.
